subject: Service-level template — proposed adjustments and credit matrix
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Meyers <lauren.meyers@astermedical.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Service-level template — proposed adjustments and credit matrix

Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for the productive call Friday. Per our discussion, attached is Redwood's current SLA template (Redwood_SLA_v1.2.pdf) with the sections I flagged for easier negotiation: uptime target, monthly credit schedule, and maintenance/exception carve-outs. High-level proposal:

- Uptime (monthly): 99.95% by default for hosted inference.
- Monthly service credits: tiered schedule capped at 10% of that month’s invoice for a single region.
- Latency objective: P95 ≤ 350ms for standard model endpoints (we can carve out very long-tail agent workloads).
- Planned maintenance & region-level emergency mitigation carve-outs included in section 4.3.

I know Aster’s procurement asked about 99.99% uptime and a higher credits cap. Happy to discuss trade-offs — increasing the uptime commitment materially increases reserved capacity and cost for both sides. If you can share Aster’s expected request volume profile and peak concurrency, we can model a targeted exception or a phased SLA (e.g., baseline 99.95% with a 6-month review).

Attached: Redwood_SLA_v1.2.pdf (redlines), sample credit matrix (placeholder).

Next steps: would you like a tracked-redlines version from us with a counterproposal on uptime/credits, or do you prefer to send your redlines first?

Thanks,
Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Americas
Redwood Inference
viv.k@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: Redwood_SLA_v1.2.pdf (PDF, 82KB)

From: Lauren Meyers <lauren.meyers@astermedical.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <dcho@astermedical.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service-level template — proposed adjustments and credit matrix

Vivek —

Thanks for sending this over. We reviewed with Legal and Infrastructure. A few initial asks:

1) Uptime: Aster needs 99.99% monthly for our core patient-facing inference endpoints (high availability is a regulatory preference given SLA for clinical triage).
2) Credits: we cannot accept a 10% cap — propose a sliding scale up to 25% for severe multi-day incidents affecting production in a region.
3) Carve-outs: we want narrower maintenance windows and explicit notification timelines (48 hours for planned maintenance, 1 hour for emergency maintenance notifications where possible).

I've attached Aster_SLA_redlines.docx with line-by-line comments and a short appendix with our traffic-profile and peak-concurrency numbers. We appreciate Redwood’s position on cost — if you can provide a path to 99.99% for the core endpoints (even as an add-on for those specific endpoints) and a firm incident response SLA, we can likely make a commercial concession elsewhere in the contract.

Would you like us to mark which endpoints are "core" vs "non-core" for this purpose? We can send that immediately.

Best,
Lauren

--
Lauren Meyers
VP, Digital Platforms
Aster Medical
lauren.meyers@astermedical.com
Attachment: Aster_SLA_redlines.docx (DOCX, 43KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Meyers <lauren.meyers@astermedical.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service-level template — proposed adjustments and credit matrix

Lauren —

Appreciate the clear feedback and the redlines. I pasted the most salient items below and proposed compromises so we can move quickly:

- Uptime: Aster asks 99.99% for core endpoints. Compromise: we can offer 99.98% for designated core endpoints as a premium add-on for the first 6 months, with a joint review at month 6 tied to traffic and incident history. Achieving 99.99% consistently requires dedicated reserved capacity and cross-region replication that will add to your committed spend.

- Credits: rather than an uncapped 25%, we propose a tiered credit schedule: 0–4.99 hours downtime => 5% credit, 5–24.99 hours => 15% credit, >25 hours => 25% credit (capped at 25% per month). To address your concern about multi-day incidents, we can add an escalation path and faster incident response (see below).

- Maintenance notification: we can narrow planned maintenance windows to a max of 4 hours and commit to 48-hour advance notice for non-emergency maintenance. Emergency maintenance will have a best-effort 1-hour notice; we will provide a post-incident report within 72 hours.

- Incident response: we can commit to an initial response within 1 hour for Sev1 incidents and a mitigation timeline target of 4 hours to put a temporary mitigation (e.g., fall back to compatible model variant / region failover) in place.

If that sounds like a starting point I’ll ask Laura (legal) to prepare tracked redlines and Karthik to confirm the commercial delta for the reserved capacity add-on. Can you confirm which endpoints you want designated as core (or send the list), and whether Aster would consider a 12-month minimum for the premium SLA?

Next: attaching a proposed credit matrix spreadsheet so you can see the math.

Thanks,
Vivek

--

Vivek / Laura —

Quick internal: I reviewed Vivek's suggested compromise and Aster's redlines. Given the strategic value and the potential ARR, I'm OK approving the premium add-on route with these guardrails:

- Approve offering 99.98% for designated core endpoints as a paid add-on for a minimum 12-month term.
- Approve tiered credits: 0–4.99h = 5%, 5–24.99h = 15%, >25h = 25% (cap 25%/month).
- Approve narrower planned maintenance notification (48h) and 1-hour best-effort emergency notice.
- Require: Aster signs up for regionally redundant deployment within 60 days of go-live OR accepts a documented risk statement that performance to 99.98% depends on reserved capacity.

Action items:
- Laura: please prepare tracked redlines to accept those terms and draft an addendum for the premium SLA option.
- Vivek: send a summary to Lauren with the proposed commercial delta for the reserved capacity (expected incremental monthly cost estimate).

If Aster pushes back on the 12-month minimum we can consider 6 months with a higher price premium.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
